subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The boundary separating one drainage basin from another is the:
questions.explain: The watershed is the ridge of high land marking the edge of a drainage basin.

questions.q: A delta forms where a river:
options: Deposits its load as it enters a sea or lake
Begins at its source on a mountain
questions.explain: Deltas form where a river deposits sediment as it slows on entering still water.

questions.q: A flood hydrograph with a short lag time and high peak discharge usually indicates:
options: A gentle slow response, e.g. forested basin
A rapid flashy response, e.g. urban or impermeable basin
questions.explain: A short lag time and high peak show water reaching the river quickly, raising flood risk.

questions.q: Which is an example of SOFT engineering flood management?
questions.explain: Soft engineering, like planting trees and zoning land use, works with natural processes.

questions.q: Dissolved minerals carried invisibly in the water are transported by:
questions.explain: In solution, dissolved load is carried chemically within the water.

questions.q: The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries is the:
questions.explain: A drainage basin is the whole area of land drained by a river system.

questions.q: On the outside of a meander bend, the river mainly:
options: Erodes, forming a steep river cliff
Deposits sediment forming a slip-off slope
questions.explain: Faster flow on the outer bend erodes the bank, creating a river cliff.

questions.q: Which is a HUMAN cause of increased river flooding?
options: Building on floodplains and creating impermeable surfaces
questions.explain: Urbanisation adds impermeable surfaces and drains, speeding water into rivers.

questions.q: Transport in which small particles bounce along the river bed is called:
questions.explain: Saltation is the bouncing or hopping of small particles along the bed.

questions.q: Erosion caused by the sheer force of fast-moving water hitting and pushing into cracks in the bank is called:
questions.explain: Hydraulic action is the force of water compressing air in cracks, weakening rock.

questions.q: Natural raised banks of sediment along the edges of a river channel are called:
questions.explain: Levees are raised banks built up by repeated deposition during floods.

options: The neck of a meander is cut through and the loop is cut off
questions.explain: Erosion eventually cuts through a meander neck, leaving the loop as an ox-bow lake.
